meta.title: AWS Solutions Architect Associate — Deep Revision Guide
meta.author: Sandeep Tiwari
meta.summary: A deep AWS Solutions Architect Associate revision guide focused on architecture decisions, trade-offs, reliability, scalability, storage, networking, security, databases, disaster recovery and real-world scenarios.

thumbnail.alt: AWS Solutions Architect Associate architecture revision guide

content.tle: AWS Solutions Architect Associate — Deep Revision Guide
content.smr: Do not memorize AWS services independently. Think in terms of requirement, constraint, architecture pattern, AWS service and trade-off. The goal of SAA preparation is to identify the architectural decision hidden inside the question.
content.p: Almost every AWS SAA question can be reduced to a small set of architectural requirements. Before selecting a service, identify what the application actually needs.

list.item: What type of storage is required?
Is the workload stateful or stateless?
What are the RPO and RTO requirements?

content.quote: SAA shortcut: Requirement → Constraint → AWS service → Trade-off.
content.p: Suppose an application must support thousands of users and remain available if one Availability Zone fails.

list.item: Place instances across multiple Availability Zones.
Move persistent state into managed services.

content.p: A common AWS architecture is Application Load Balancer plus EC2 Auto Scaling Group across multiple Availability Zones, with a managed database and externalized session/cache state.

img.alt: Highly available AWS web application architecture
img.caption: Typical multi-AZ web application architecture

content.p: An AWS Region is a geographic area containing multiple isolated Availability Zones. Regions are independent failure domains and are often selected based on latency, regulatory requirements, service availability and disaster recovery strategy.
An Availability Zone is one or more discrete data centers with independent infrastructure inside an AWS Region.

list.item: AZ failure should not necessarily cause application failure.
Resources can be distributed across AZs.
AZs within a Region are connected using low-latency networking.

content.p: Edge locations are used by services such as CloudFront to bring content closer to users and reduce latency.

Amazon EC2 provides virtual compute capacity. In SAA questions, EC2 is usually not the difficult part. The important architectural question is how EC2 instances are deployed, scaled, secured and made fault tolerant.
A standard production architecture uses an Application Load Balancer in front of an Auto Scaling Group.

list.item: User sends request to the application endpoint.
Auto Scaling launches or terminates instances according to demand.

img.alt: EC2 Application Load Balancer Auto Scaling architecture
img.caption: EC2 + ALB + Auto Scaling

content.p: If all EC2 instances exist in one Availability Zone, an AZ-level failure can make the entire application unavailable.
Deploying instances across multiple AZs allows the application to continue operating when one AZ becomes unavailable.

list.item: Works with load balancer health checks.

content.p: Stateless application servers do not depend on local memory or local disk for information that must survive another request.
This is important because Auto Scaling may create a new instance at any time and the load balancer may send a user's next request to another instance.

list.item: Database state → RDS or another database service.

content.quote: Good scalable architecture treats compute as disposable and persistent state as external.

img.alt: Stateless application with Redis and persistent storage
img.caption: Stateless application with externalized state

content.p: Elastic Block Store provides persistent block storage for EC2 instances. It behaves like a virtual disk attached to an EC2 instance.

list.item: Persistent beyond instance termination depending on configuration.
Useful for operating systems and application data.

content.p: Instance Store provides physically attached temporary storage. Data is lost when the instance is stopped, terminated or otherwise loses the underlying host according to the instance lifecycle.
content.quote: Instance Store = temporary high-performance local storage.
content.p: Elastic File System provides managed shared file storage that can be mounted by multiple compute instances.

list.item: Multiple EC2 instances need the same file system.

content.p: S3 is object storage. It is not a normal mounted block disk and should be preferred when applications need durable object storage rather than traditional file-system semantics.
Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 and understands HTTP and HTTPS requests.
TLS can terminate at the Application Load Balancer. The ALB decrypts the request and forwards it to backend targets according to the configured architecture.
Server Name Indication allows a TLS endpoint to support multiple certificates for multiple hostnames on the same listener.
Amazon RDS provides managed relational databases. The major SAA distinction is between Multi-AZ deployment, Read Replicas and cross-Region disaster recovery.
Multi-AZ is primarily an availability and failover mechanism.

list.item: Provides standby infrastructure in another AZ.
Standby is not primarily intended for read scaling.

content.p: Read Replicas are primarily used to scale read workloads.

list.item: Applications can send read traffic to replicas.
Multiple replicas can support read-heavy workloads.

content.p: A cross-Region replica can be used as part of a disaster recovery architecture and can also provide geographically closer read access.
content.quote: Exam distinction: Multi-AZ = availability. Read Replica = read scaling. Cross-Region replication = geographic resilience or locality.

img.alt: RDS Multi AZ versus Read Replica architecture
img.caption: RDS Multi-AZ and Read Replica decision

content.p: Amazon Aurora is a managed relational database engine compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL.
Aurora separates compute from distributed storage. Its storage layer is designed to provide high durability and replication across Availability Zones.

list.item: Aurora Replicas can provide read scaling.

content.p: ElastiCache provides managed in-memory caching using engines such as Redis-compatible and Memcached technologies.
content.quote: Cache is normally an optimization layer, not the authoritative source of durable business data.
content.p: Amazon S3 is highly durable object storage and one of the most important services for SAA.

list.item: S3 Intelligent-Tiering → access pattern is unpredictable.
S3 Standard-IA → infrequently accessed but rapidly retrievable data.
S3 One Zone-IA → infrequently accessed data where single-AZ storage is acceptable.
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval → archive data requiring rapid retrieval.
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval → archival data with flexible retrieval time.
S3 Glacier Deep Archive → very long-term archival data.
SSE-KMS → encryption integrated with AWS KMS and key policies.
Client-side encryption → encryption performed before data reaches S3.

content.p: Versioning maintains multiple versions of objects. It helps protect against accidental deletion and accidental overwrites.
Lifecycle rules automatically transition objects between storage classes or expire objects after a defined period.
CloudFront is AWS's content delivery network. It caches content at edge locations closer to users.

list.item: Integrate with S3 and other origins.

content.p: A common secure architecture uses CloudFront as the public distribution endpoint while keeping the S3 bucket private.
Origin Access Control allows CloudFront to access the S3 origin without making the bucket publicly accessible.

img.alt: CloudFront with private S3 origin using Origin Access Control
img.caption: CloudFront + private S3 + Origin Access Control

content.p: Route 53 is AWS's highly available DNS service.
Route 53 health checks can be used to direct traffic to a healthy primary endpoint and fail over to another endpoint when the primary becomes unavailable.
Latency-based routing directs users toward the Region expected to provide the lowest latency.
Amazon Elastic Container Registry stores container images.
Amazon Elastic Container Service orchestrates containers.
AWS Fargate provides serverless compute for containers. The customer does not manage the underlying EC2 instances.
Replace or update instances gradually while maintaining part of the old version during deployment.
Maintain two environments. The old environment is Blue and the new environment is Green. Traffic is switched to Green after validation.
Send a small percentage of traffic to the new version before gradually increasing traffic.

list.item: Real users validate the new version.
Traffic percentage can be increased gradually.

content.p: A Virtual Private Cloud provides an isolated logical network in AWS.
A subnet is considered public when its route table provides a route toward an Internet Gateway.
A private subnet does not provide a direct route to an Internet Gateway. Private resources can use a NAT Gateway for outbound Internet access when required.
An Internet Gateway provides connectivity between a VPC and the public Internet for resources configured with appropriate routes and public addressing.
NAT Gateway allows resources in private subnets to initiate outbound Internet connections without allowing unsolicited inbound connections from the Internet.

list.item: Allows rules rather than explicit deny rules.

content.quote: Security Group = stateful resource-level firewall. Network ACL = stateless subnet-level firewall.
content.p: IAM controls authentication and authorization for AWS resources.

list.item: Roles → identities assumed by users, applications or AWS services.

content.p: Grant only the permissions required to perform the intended operation. Avoid broad permissions such as unrestricted access when a specific resource and action can be defined.
Applications running on EC2 should normally obtain AWS permissions through an IAM role rather than storing long-lived access keys inside the instance.
Disaster recovery questions usually revolve around two numbers: Recovery Point Objective and Recovery Time Objective.
Recovery Point Objective answers: How much data loss is acceptable?
Recovery Time Objective answers: How long can the system remain unavailable?
Lowest operational complexity and generally lowest cost, but usually requires the longest recovery time.
Keep the minimum critical infrastructure running and scale it during a disaster.
Maintain a smaller but operational version of the production environment that can quickly be scaled up.
Run production workloads simultaneously in multiple locations. This can provide the lowest recovery time but generally has the highest cost and operational complexity.
content.quote: Faster RTO and lower RPO usually require more infrastructure, replication and operational complexity.
content.p: High availability focuses on keeping the system operational despite failures.
Scalability focuses on handling increasing workload.
content.quote: Availability asks: Can the system survive failure? Scalability asks: Can the system handle more workload?
content.p: Increase the capacity of a single machine by using more CPU, memory or other resources.
Add more machines or application instances.

list.item: Horizontal scaling generally provides better elasticity.
Stateless design makes horizontal scaling easier.
Keep large files out of application servers.

content.p: Instead of memorizing hundreds of services, classify the requirement.

list.item: Need relational database → RDS or Aurora.
Need Layer 4 load balancing → Network Load Balancer.
Need DNS-based failover → Route 53 failover routing.
Need private outbound Internet access → NAT Gateway.

content.hd2: Question: Application must survive an AZ failure
content.p: Use multiple Availability Zones and distribute the workload across them.
Consider RDS Multi-AZ rather than simply adding a Read Replica.
content.hd2: Question: Database has too many read requests
content.p: Consider Read Replicas and caching.
content.hd2: Question: Users around the world experience high latency for static files
content.p: Consider CloudFront.
content.hd2: Question: Private EC2 instances need outbound Internet access
content.p: Use a NAT Gateway in an appropriate public subnet and route private subnet traffic through it.
content.hd2: Question: Multiple EC2 instances require the same files
content.p: Consider EFS when shared file-system semantics are required.
content.hd2: Question: Store millions of images cheaply and durably
content.p: S3 is generally the appropriate object-storage service.
content.hd2: Question: Application servers need user sessions but must scale horizontally
content.p: Externalize session state, commonly using an appropriate managed cache such as ElastiCache.
content.hd2: Question: Need the lowest possible recovery time
content.p: Consider Warm Standby or Multi-Site Active/Active depending on the required RTO, RPO, cost and complexity.
AWS SAA becomes easier when cloud architecture is viewed through distributed-systems principles.

Any instance, disk, network connection, Availability Zone or even Region can eventually fail. Architecture should therefore avoid single points of failure when availability requirements demand redundancy.
If compute nodes do not own important state, they can be added or removed freely.
content.hd2: Replication Improves Availability but Adds Complexity
content.p: Replication can improve durability and availability but introduces consistency, replication lag and operational considerations.
Cached data can become stale. The architecture must define acceptable freshness and invalidation behavior.
Queues and event-driven architectures allow producers and consumers to operate independently and absorb traffic spikes.
When several answers appear technically valid, eliminate answers that violate the strongest requirement in the question.

list.item: Eliminate architectures that violate the explicit availability requirement.
Eliminate solutions that introduce unnecessary operational management.
Eliminate solutions that are significantly more expensive when cost is explicitly constrained.
Eliminate solutions that do not meet the required RPO or RTO.
Eliminate architectures that create an obvious single point of failure.
Prefer managed AWS services when they satisfy the requirement.
Prefer the simplest architecture that fully satisfies the requirements.

content.quote: SAA questions usually ask for the BEST architecture, not merely an architecture that works.
content.p: Before finalizing an architecture, mentally run through the following checklist.

list.item: Is compute distributed across Availability Zones?
What happens when one instance fails?
What happens when one AZ fails?
What are the RPO and RTO?
What happens if the Region fails?
Is the solution more complicated than necessary?
Is there a cheaper managed AWS service that satisfies the same requirement?

content.p: The most important SAA skill is not memorizing service definitions. It is recognizing architectural patterns from requirements.

list.item: High availability → remove single points of failure.
Performance → cache, scale reads, reduce distance and use CDN.
Durability → replicate and back up data.
Security → least privilege, private networking and encryption.
DR → choose the strategy based on RPO, RTO and cost.
Cost optimization → choose the simplest service that meets requirements.
Operational excellence → prefer managed services when appropriate.

content.quote: Think like an architect: identify the failure, identify the bottleneck, identify the state, identify the required recovery objective, and then select the AWS service that solves that exact problem.
